one_line: Cheap because its core online checkout button has stalled and rivals are taking share. Profits and buybacks are real, so the fall is partly fair and partly overdone.

why_fell.evidence: Branded checkout volume grew 1% in Q3 2026 and has stayed at 1-2% for four quarters. Barclays expects 1-2% in Q4. This is PayPal's most profitable product.

why_fell.reason: Losing share to Apple Pay, Shop Pay and Google Pay
why_fell.evidence: Citizens said PayPal is losing share. Barclays cites losses to Apple Pay and Shop Pay. Canaccord says the button is under pressure as rivals streamline payment.

why_fell.reason: CEO fired and a reset year
why_fell.evidence: The board replaced CEO Alex Chriss with HP's Enrique Lores on 3 Feb 2026, saying execution pace was below expectations. Shares fell about 17-20% that day on weak guidance.
Stripe and Advent bid $60.50 a share (about $53 billion) in July. Bloomberg reported on 28 Aug they dropped the pursuit, and shares fell up to 16% premarket.
why_fell.source: Bloomberg via The Star / Irish Times

for_unfair.point: Q3 2026 profit beat: adjusted earnings per share rose 8% to $1.45 and full-year guidance rose to about $5.60. At $56 the stock is about 10 times that.
Buybacks are large: $1.5 billion in Q3 and $6.0 billion over 12 months. Shares outstanding fell to 837 million from 920 million at end of 2025, about 9% in nine months.
Outside buyers saw value: a Stripe and Advent group bid $60.50 a share in July. The board called it too low. Lores says the strategy is starting to show in results.

for_fair.point: Sales growth is 2% (1% ignoring currency) and missed forecasts by about 1.5%. Margin dollars grew only 2%. Take rate fell 6 basis points as PayPal spends to win checkout and buy-now-pay-later.

Barclays cut to Underweight (target $53) on 29 Oct 2026. It says the turnaround plan overlaps with years-old initiatives and agentic commerce could erode checkout buttons further. Morgan Stanley sees it as a multi-year overhang.
Cash flow is weakening: free cash flow fell 17% and adjusted free cash flow fell 10% in Q3. Restructuring cost was $255 million versus $69 million a year earlier.

what_market_fears: Wallets built into phones and stores, and AI shopping agents, make the PayPal button unnecessary. Then the highest-margin volume shrinks while buybacks only hide it.
what_would_prove_it_wrong: Branded checkout growth returning above 3-4% for two quarters, take rate stabilising, and AI-chat checkout (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google) showing real volume while buybacks continue at this pace.
next_date_to_watch: Q4 2026 results and 2027 guidance, likely early Feb 2027 (date not confirmed). Q4 guide for branded checkout is 1-2% growth.

flag.note: Net revenue is still up 2% to $8.6 billion and margin dollars up 2%, so sales have not shrunk. But branded checkout is near zero growth, so it is close.

not_found: Did not independently verify the 10 times cash-flow figure after stock pay. Agentic checkout volume numbers for 2026 not found (only partnership announcements). Price targets from Morgan Stanley and others not read at source. Earnings-call text was seen as search summary only.
